title_candidates: Hugging Face shows how to test whether agents can use your tools
summary: Hugging Face's agentic benchmarking post argues that success is not enough: track how many steps, tokens, errors, and detours an agent needs.

primary_source.title: Is it agentic enough? Benchmarking open models on your own tooling
primary_source.author: Hugging Face
key_facts: Hugging Face published an agent-focused benchmark post using transformers as a case study.
The post argues that tool maintainers should measure not only whether an agent gets the right answer, but how much work it took.
The benchmark varies model, library revision, task, and the kind of context given to the agent.
The post tracks metrics such as match rate, median time, token use, errors, and behavior markers.

prerequisites: A tool, document workflow, or small repo you want an AI agent to use

steps.instruction: Pick three tiny tasks an agent should be able to complete with your tool.
Run the same agent on each task and record whether it succeeded.
Also record how many turns it took, whether it read the right docs, and whether it used deprecated or fragile paths.
Add one clearer example, command, or short guide where the agent struggled.
Rerun the same three tasks and keep the change only if success improves without adding confusing extra context.

references.title: Is it agentic enough? Benchmarking open models on your own tooling
references.author: Hugging Face
